**Fieldnote turns a technician's voice note into a finished service report before they are back in the van.**

## The problem

Field technicians spend 45–70 minutes a day writing service reports, usually at the end of the day and from memory. Details go missing, invoices wait, and warranty claims fail for lack of evidence.

## The product

After each job the technician speaks for a minute and takes photos. Fieldnote produces a structured report — work done, parts, readings, follow-ups — matched to the customer's equipment record and sent to the office system for approval.

- Works offline; syncs when the phone has signal.
- Understands German, French, Italian and English trade vocabulary.
- Integrates with the three most common field-service systems in the region.

## Pilot results

| Metric | Before | With Fieldnote |
|---|---:|---:|
| Report writing per technician per day | 58 min | 11 min |
| Reports with missing parts or readings | 23 % | 4 % |
| Days from job to invoice | 9.5 | 1.8 |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Technicians review every report before it is sent. Fieldnote never invents readings: anything it could not hear is left empty and flagged.

## What we ask for

1. An eight-week pilot with 10–20 of your technicians, free of charge.
2. Access to a test instance of your field-service system.
3. One reviewer in the service office during the pilot.

**Pricing:** CHF 39 per technician per month, annual contract; volume pricing above 50 technicians. **Team:** founded 2025 in Winterthur by Lara Meier (service operations) and Yusuf Demir (speech recognition); eight employees. **Contact:** lara@fieldnote.example · +41 52 000 00 00
